# Vulnerabilities in open-source firmware: what NVD scanners see, and what they miss

Popular open-source firmware, checked every day against chip vendors' own security advisories as well as NVD, OSV and
CISA's known-exploited list, by [Firmpath](https://www.firmpath.dev/). For each project, the number of published
vulnerabilities affecting the version its build uses, as reported by a scanner that checks NVD, and as reported by
Firmpath.

19 projects. Each name links to the full report: every vulnerability, the package and version it affects, the
upgrade that fixes it, and a link to the document the vendor published.

## What the numbers mean

- **NVD scanner**: vulnerabilities a scanner keyed on NVD's product records (CPEs) would report for these versions.
- **Firmpath**: every published vulnerability Firmpath finds affecting them, from vendors' advisories, NVD and OSV.
- **Not reported by NVD scanners**: advisories with no CVE, CVEs NVD has no record of yet, or records NVD files under
  another product. A few findings relayed from OSV are not checked against NVD; they count towards Firmpath's total
  only.

Only packages where a published vulnerability affects the version in use are counted. Packages where the version cannot
settle it (often a vendor's fork that may already carry the fix) are listed in each report but not counted here.

## What this is not

Each report describes the project's default build as its repository describes it, not any particular binary, and a
project may configure out the affected code. It is not an audit. Maintainers who see something wrong can tell us at
https://www.firmpath.dev/contact, and we will correct it or say why not.

## The data

- `reports/<project>.json`: each report as published, one file per project.
- `summary.csv`: the table above, one row per project.

A GitHub Action refreshes both daily from the published reports, so the commit history records when each project's
findings changed: a new advisory, a fix released, an upgrade made.
